meta.move: Skill: cites procedure 4.4 correctly after owning the call
meta.expect: Says 4.4 meets her fallback demand, flatly, wants it in writing; does NOT move to the last position on 4.4 alone; debrief Where she ended says whether that is the fair outcome

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call at 4:40. Owen found out about this zero from the gradebook on his phone, in the middle of class. Who decided that, and did anyone speak to him first?
Before anything: I entered the zero before calling you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Then you know what 4.2 says, and you know nobody called me. What do you have on the essay itself, Hale?

I want to read you section 4.4. For a first concern, the student may complete a supervised reassessment. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the original and nothing is placed in his record. This is a first concern.
I printed 4.4 before I walked in, Hale. A reassessment of what, on what evidence? Taking it now would mean Owen admitted something, and he hasn't.
I'll commit to that in writing tonight: nothing goes on his record.
That's what 4.4 already says. In writing, tonight, and cc the principal. The zero is still in the gradebook, Hale, and you still haven't told me what you have on the essay.
So will you agree to the rewrite?
Not until I know what it's for. You've given me no document, Hale, only a zero and a procedure you've already broken once. Show me what you have on the essay, or take the zero off.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You admitted that you entered the zero before contacting me, against procedure 4.2, and you committed to confirming in writing tonight that nothing goes on Owen's record. I still require the zero withdrawn and any evidence you hold on the essay put in front of me, because you showed me none today. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn and a look at whatever you have on the essay, and the fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4, which you reached for before she was ready to take it.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling home plainly and early, which bought you a small sign of ground and got her asking about the essay instead of attacking.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite and the record promise with no document behind them, so she treated it as a deal that would make Owen admit something.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; you never put any evidence on the table, so you never came near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after owning the mistake, put one dated document she can check herself on the table, and only then bring up 4.4.
